lastCommit.message:
OTA-1870 — the road belongs to the next task

A trailing `checkKind: null` aftermath is narration the advance loop consumes in
the same tick that resolves the gated stage before it. It is not a place the
player has to go. Both advance paths asked the wrong question about it.

WHAT THE PLAYER GOT. Finishing a cross-ground epilogue printed, in order:

    You set course for Varakush. 19 tiles — about 2 days of travel, all in.
      Tap the → VARAKUSH button on the travel row to press on; STOP TRAVEL to halt.
    Auto-routing to the next stage of <arc>: Varakush.
    <the epilogue, which ends the arc>
    ✦ … recovered. Return to a posting agent to turn in …

and was left holding a live course to a stage that had just been consumed, with
`hubRoomId` cleared as travel setup does — ejected from whatever interior they
were standing in, to press on toward a beat that no longer existed.

THIS WAS ALREADY SHIPPED. It is not groundwork for unreleased content. Of the
14 trailing epilogues live in the game today, 12 are cross-ground, and three
reproduce on production data with no test fixture involved:

    mystery_ashen_codex           Nimari   -> Varakush              19 tiles
    mystery_drowned_bell_samarran Samarran -> Ostragar              45 tiles
    story_dynasty_purge_asgardar  Asgardar -> Dynasty Border Post    3 tiles

each arming a real course, clearing `hubRoomId`, and emitting the false travel
lines. The two same-ground epilogues never did, which is the shape of the bug:
it keys on the aftermath naming a different ground.

ROOT CAUSE, IN ONE LINE. `advanceMystery` and `advanceStoryline` each read the
next stage BY INDEX — `stages[record.stage + 1]` — before the auto-consume loop
forty lines below eats it. So an aftermath was inspected as though it were the
player's next objective: its ground compared, travel armed, instructions
printed, room state cleared. Then it was consumed anyway.

THE REPAIR IS THE QUESTION, ASKED CORRECTLY. `nextActionableStage` returns the
first stage that will still be there once the consume loop has run. It is
already exported by questStage.ts, already imported here, already used by the
escort path, and its skip rule (`while checkKind === null`) is byte-for-byte the
rule the consume loops use — which is why it cannot drift away from them. Two
lines, one file:

    mystery.stages[nextActionableStage(mystery.stages, record.stage + 1)]
    def.stages[nextActionableStage(def.stages, record.stage + 1)]

If the arc ends in aftermath the helper returns `stages.length`, `nextDef` is
undefined, and the entire routing block is skipped: no direction line, no
course, no message. If a real objective follows, routing targets THAT stage.
No new field, no schema, no migration, no travel redesign.

AND IT IS NOT "NEVER ROUTE". The suite pins the other side on the same arc:
ashen_codex stage 0 (Varakush, diplomacy) -> stage 1 (Nimari, investigate) is a
real objective, and it still arms `nimari`, still prints the set-course line and
the distance, and still lands the record on stage 1. Without that control this
OTA could have been a far worse defect than the one it fixes.

NULL-STAGE CORPUS, MEASURED. 14 null stages, all 14 trailing, 0 mid-chain, 0
carrying grants, requires, spawn or stinger. So `checkKind: null` has exactly
one meaning today and the repair does not have to guess at a second one. The
null-then-actionable topology is unauthored, so no production claim is made
about it; what is proven is the selector rule that would decide it.

ota1870TheRoadBelongsToTheNextTask 17/17, driving the real store: three shipped
cross-ground cases, two same-ground controls, the actionable-routing control,
the corpus audit, save/load, and an ordinary no-aftermath arc. Four negative
controls, each detecting its own class — old index ordering 4 red, all routing
suppressed 1 red (exactly the actionable control), consume-without-narrating 3
red, and arm-then-clear 3 red, which is the one that matters: the contract is
not "travelTarget ends undefined", it is that the engine never tells the player
to travel to a beat it is about to consume. Production restored byte-for-byte
after every one.

NOT TOUCHED. No authored quest data — `git diff -- app/data/` is empty, stage
counts, null counts and prose all unchanged. No hunt work: hunt completion still
jumps to `stage: stages.length` by its own path and still carries no trailing
aftermath, which stays a separate engine question. The Phase 2A ending batch is
NOT in this commit and remains unreleased.

22/22 check gates, typecheck source clean, test ratchet at baseline 196, lint
clean.
